### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c120dbdfb81743a172622b7aec6d81bb9f2ed9bf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Seat read — and ⛔ NO at-tier subagent is owed here, by the rule's own words

Written by the `domain:spec` execution seat 1 (`session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`) at 2026-09-22T23:03Z, on head `cbb3521fe5`.

### Why there is no isolated review on this PR, ⛔ and why that is not a skipped step

`origin/main:.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md` decides it, and it decides it **by surface, not by lane** — its own words:

> 欠不欠**按面判** ⛔ **不按车道**:diff 碰下列任一面即欠达档复核 … 复核面 = 出货给用户或 agent 的五处:`content/docs/**`、`apps/docs/**`、CHANGELOG/`.changeset` 散文 … 加已发布 schema(`packages/spec/src/**` **非测试**)与 governed 规则文本 … **五面皆不碰 ⇒ CI 加席位自读 ⛔ 不起第二个 agent**

This diff is **one file**, `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts`, `+281/−0`. Against the five:

| surface | this diff |
|:--|:--|
| `content/docs/**` | no |
| `apps/docs/**` | no |
| CHANGELOG / `.changeset` prose | no |
| published schema — `packages/spec/src/**`, **non-test** | no: the path is `packages/spec/scripts/`, ⛔ not `src/`, **and** it is a `.test.ts` |
| governed rule text | no |

⇒ 五面皆不碰 ⇒ **CI plus a seat read, and ⛔ not a second agent.** Spawning one here would be the seat ignoring a rule to look thorough.

⚠️ **A correction this seat owes on its own record:** two earlier notes on sibling PRs described a review as owed 「by the lane rule (C6)」. The governing text says ⛔ 不按车道 in as many words. Those reviews were still owed — each of those diffs touched a listed surface (`.changeset` prose, or `packages/spec/src/**` non-test, or `content/docs/**`) — so ⛔ nothing was over-dispatched; what was wrong was the stated basis, and it is corrected here rather than left standing.

### The seat read — structure, ⛔ not a verdict on behaviour

Read at head at 2026-09-22T23:03Z:

- **Scope holds exactly.** One file, `+281/−0`, no other path in the diff.
- ⭐ **The fifth box copies `src`, it does not link it.** `fs.cpSync(PKG/src → box/src, { recursive: true })`, with `symlinkSync` left for the other entries only — the shape of the four boxes that already do this. ⇒ the fixture's synthetic `strictObject` lives in the box's **private** copy, so route A (a synthetic schema written into the real `src`, which `files[]` would ship to consumers via `src/**/*.zod.ts`) is avoided **by construction**, ⛔ not by care.
- ⭐ **The substitution is anchored, and the anchor is guarded.** A regex pins `strictObject` as one function declaration, and the fixture asserts it matches before substituting, with a message that says the declaration has moved. ⇒ if the anchor drifts the fixture goes red loudly, ⛔ it does not silently substitute nothing and pass.
- **Both directions are pinned.** Alongside the positive assertions the case carries negative ones — the output must **not** contain the compliant-looking prescription line. ⚠️ That is the point of this card: the failure direction is 「reads as compliant」, a defeated leg **waives** the deletion rather than adding a 「no evidence」 row, so a one-directional pin would not have caught it.

⛔ This is a reading of the diff's shape. It is ⛔ not a claim that the pin fires — that is what the round's own ablation evidence and CI have to show, and neither is in yet.

### What is still outstanding on this PR

- The round's `os-dev-report` has not arrived; ⛔ nothing here is taken as verified until it does and is checked against GitHub.
- CI at 2026-09-22T23:03Z: **32 check names — 8 success, 3 skipped, 0 failure, 21 still running.** ⚠️ Running is **NOT MEASURED**, ⛔ not a pass.
- The changeset route is the seat's to settle once the gate reports: this diff touches one test file and no package's `files[]` surface, but ⛔ the seat applies no label on a guess — it reads the gate's own job log first, as it did on the sibling PR.

## ⛔ Correcting this seat's own note `5785719474` — an at-tier review IS owed here, and it is being arranged

Written by the `domain:spec` execution seat 1 (`session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`) at 2026-09-22T23:06Z. The earlier note said ⛔ no isolated review was owed on this PR. **That was wrong.** ⛔ Nothing in the diff changed; what was wrong was the rule this seat read.

### What the earlier note got wrong

It applied `references/contract-review.md`'s five-surface test — 「欠不欠按面判 ⛔ 不按车道 … 五面皆不碰 ⇒ CI 加席位自读 ⛔ 不起第二个 agent」 — and stopped there. The surface reading itself is right: this diff is one `.test.ts` under `packages/spec/scripts/`, so it touches none of the five.

⭐ **But that clause is the OTHER-lane case, and the file it points at says so in as many words.** `origin/main:scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs`, the C6 block, quoting the maintainer's own rule as restated on **#18536**:

> The lane rule (the maintainer's …) owes the contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` **in the spec and skills lanes on EVERY delivered round, `Clause-②: yes` or `no`**, and **in no other lane**: there the three landing pre-checks and the gates are the whole bar, ⛔ no default-tier "self-review" record is demanded and **⛔ no at-tier subagent is spawned**.

⇒ 「⛔ 不起第二个 agent」 is what applies **outside** spec and skills. **Inside** them the review is owed every round, whatever the surface and whatever the declaration says.

C6's machine half reads it off the card: 「on a `Clause-②: no` pair whose CARD sits in a lane that owes the review on every round (`laneOwesReview`, **read off the card's `domain:*` labels**)」. Measured at 2026-09-22T23:06Z: **card #18865 carries `domain:spec`.** Absent record ⇒ C6 renders **a FINDING row and exit 4**, ⛔ not an advisory.

### How this seat got it wrong, recorded rather than smoothed over

Two messages ago this seat "corrected" itself in the wrong direction: it had described a sibling PR's review as owed 「by the lane rule (C6)」, then read `contract-review.md` alone and declared that wording mistaken because that file says ⛔ 不按车道. **The lane rule was the right citation all along** — it is a maintainer ruling, which outranks a 细则 in the priority order, and C6 is its machine half.

⇒ the error was reading one reference and not the rule it points at, then being confident about the result. ⛔ Neither the first statement nor its "correction" was measured against `check-clause2-carriers.mjs` until now.

⚠️ Nothing landed on that mistake: the sibling PRs each touched a listed surface too, so every review this seat dispatched was owed on both readings. The only PR where the two readings differ is **this one**, and it is being fixed before it could cost anything.

### What happens now

An isolated at-tier subagent is being dispatched against head `cbb3521fe5`, and the record it renders will be posted here in the required shape. ⛔ This seat does not self-review: it is below `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and 未达档 ⛔ 不自审 stands.

The **seat read** in `5785719474` stays on the thread as what it is — a reading of the diff's shape, useful and ⛔ not a ruling. Its five-surface table is accurate; only its conclusion was wrong.

## Contract review — PR #19754, head `cbb3521fe5eb5921277107d81c28d2e343f5792e`

Isolated at-tier contract review for the `domain:spec` lane (seat `domain:spec#1`, PM session `session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`). Subject: `objectstack-ai/objectstack` PR #19754, branch `claude/issue-18865-proof4-delivers-fixture`, head `cbb3521fe5eb5921277107d81c28d2e343f5792e`, base `main` at `c120dbdfb81743a172622b7aec6d81bb9f2ed9bf` (merge-base re-derived, identical: `git merge-base origin/main <head>` → `c120dbdfb8…`, 2026-09-22T23:07:05Z). Diff: one file, `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts`, numstat `281 0`, zero removed lines (2026-09-22T23:15:23Z). Fixes #18865.

**Tier control.** The tier served to this review is the SEAT's reading, taken from the transcript's per-request harness `model` stamps; this record's own self-report of its model is not admissible and is not offered. No fallback or overload notice was received by this review during its run. The first line's counts are left `TBD/TBD` for the seat to fill.

### Why this review exists (the lane rule, read at source)

The **surface** test does not fire: the diff touches none of `content/docs/**`, `apps/docs/**`, CHANGELOG/`.changeset` prose, published schema (`packages/spec/src/**` non-test) or governed rule text — the one path is under `packages/spec/scripts/` and is a `.test.ts`.

The review is owed by the **lane rule**. Read at `origin/main:scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs` (2026-09-22T23:07:16Z), the C6 header block says, verbatim:

> `## C6 — a record owed on this head, and none behind it (#17302; lane-keyed by #18536)` … `The lane rule (the maintainer's, restated on #18536 — 「曾经要求只有 spec 和 skills 需要 fable,其他 opus 就够了,理论上其他车道不需要契约复审」) owes the contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` in the spec and skills lanes on EVERY delivered round, `Clause-②: yes` or `no`, and in no other lane`

and, in the same file:

> `export const LANES_OWING_REVIEW = Object.freeze(['domain:spec', 'domain:skills']);`
> `export function laneOwesReview(pair) { const labels = pair?.cardLabels; if (!Array.isArray(labels)) return null; return labels.some((name) => LANES_OWING_REVIEW.includes(name)); }`

with its docblock: `Read off the CARD's labels: `domain:*` is produced by triage and lives on the card, never on the PR.` Card #18865's labels, read live (2026-09-22T23:08:41Z): `priority:p2`, `pm:dispatched`, **`domain:spec`** ⇒ `laneOwesReview` is `true` and the record is owed on this round whatever the clause-② value.

`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, read at `origin/main:scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:12282` (2026-09-22T23:07:17Z): `export const CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER = 'claude-fable-5-1';`. Its docblock carries the maintainer's 2026-09-22 ruling verbatim: 「复核档应该就是 fable 啊」 · 「某个agent临时没有fable给的特殊授权，不应该改变skills」 · 「fable 撤回卡 你来创建」, and the rule that a 429 or a missing authorization on one session is never a retirement, and that a seat not served this tier renders the review through an isolated at-tier subagent — which is what this record is.

C6 reads this record for a level-2 heading beginning `## Contract review`, the head sha as a code span (`H51_SHA_SPAN = /`([0-9a-fA-F]{7,40})`/g` in `check-half-states.mjs:12523`; `CONTRACT_REVIEW_HEADING_MARKER = /^\s*>?\s*## Contract review\b/m` at `:12511`) and a `Reviewed-by:` line (`AUTHORSHIP_KEYS = ['Implemented-by', 'Reviewed-by']`, `check-clause2-carriers.mjs:3105`). All three are present below.

### Method

- Head fetched into an owned ref `refs/review/pr-19754-head` (2026-09-22T23:06:56Z); a private detached worktree at `<scratchpad>/pr-19754/wt`, offline `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` (exit 0, 3.8 s from the store). The shared checkout was neither edited nor read for tree facts; every `main` reading is `git show origin/main:PATH` / `git grep … origin/main`.
- Gate conclusions are read from this head's GitHub check-runs only; no derived family was re-run locally. The only local executions are the harness's two new cases and the ablations of `delivers()` needed to judge the pin, in the private worktree, each restore proven by blob id.
- Nothing was posted to GitHub; no label, comment, review or ref on the remote was written.

---

## ① Derived judgments

### 1. The fifth sandbox is in the shape of the four that already work — VERIFIED

Base vs head, same file, re-derived (2026-09-22T23:15:23Z):

| reading | `origin/main` `c120dbdfb8` | head `cbb3521fe5` |
|:--|--:|--:|
| lines (`wc -l`) | 4531 | 4812 |
| `it(`/`test(` cases | 85 | 87 |
| `symlinkSync` sites | 6 | 7 |
| entry arrays `['src', 'node_modules', 'package.json']` | 1 | 1 |
| `cpSync(path.join(PKG, 'src')` sites | 4 | 5 |

The new block (head `:4695`–`:4699`): `fs.cpSync(path.join(PKG, 'scripts'), …)`, `fs.cpSync(path.join(PKG, 'src'), …, { recursive: true })`, then `for (const entry of ['node_modules', 'package.json']) fs.symlinkSync(…)` — `src` absent from the entry array, byte-for-byte the shape of the #4659 / #4725 / #5898 / #17969 boxes (`origin/main` `:3436–3439`, `:3735–3738`, `:4101–4104`, `:4365–4368`). The shared `createSandbox` (`origin/main:462–500`) is untouched: the diff removes zero lines, and the only change above line 4530 is `import { z } from 'zod';` at `:51`. The 85 pre-existing cases are untouched.

### 2. Route A is excluded by construction — VERIFIED, with controls

`origin/main:packages/spec/package.json` `files[]` carries `"src/**/*.zod.ts"` (2026-09-22T23:07:28Z), so a synthetic def in the REAL `src` would ship. The fixture's write target is `boxStrictObject = path.join(box, 'src', 'shared', 'strict-object.ts')` where `box = fixtureTree(…)` = `fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir()…)/packages/spec` and that `src` is the `cpSync` copy, not a symlink. The copied `scripts/build-schemas.ts` reaches schemas only through relative `../src/*` imports (`origin/main:build-schemas.ts:116–147`), never through the symlinked `node_modules`, so the substitution is read from the copy.

Runtime negative control, my worktree, after the intact run and after every ablation run: `git status --porcelain` → 0 lines; `packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts` blob `24c9e672f39d…` == `HEAD:` blob (2026-09-22T23:13:27Z, again 23:15:19Z). Firing control on the same subject: the LIT case exits 1 on the intact tree, which is only possible if the substituted `strictObject` WAS read by the gate — from the box copy, since the worktree copy is unchanged.

`npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts` in the private worktree (no `dist/` built here, so the absolute count is 277, not the round's 2031 on a built tree; the discriminating readings do not depend on `dist/`), 2026-09-22T23:13:16Z: POSITIVE — 204 `src/` entries, `src/shared/http.zod.ts` and `src/system/stack-server.zod.ts` present (the round's 204 is reproduced exactly). NEGATIVE — 0 entries under `scripts/`, `scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts` absent, `src/shared/strict-object.ts` (not a `.zod.ts`) absent. DARK — `src/shared/http.zod.tsx` absent. With the one changed file put back to base bytes (blob `18100c70f8…` proven on disk) the sorted list is byte-identical (`diff` exit 0), then restored to `326a8c9466…`. The round's reading holds.

### 3. The pin can fail and it discriminates — VERIFIED by my own ablations

`delivers()` at `origin/main:build-schemas.ts:1695–1709`: `return issue !== undefined && issue.message.includes(prescription);` — blob `c886e1778316b5ff8c3d1780b599e8bcb50c1970`, identical on head and main.

Intact (2026-09-22T23:13:06Z, `-t '#18865'`): **2 passed | 85 skipped (87)**, LIT 7.6 s, DARK 9.2 s.

**Ablation A** (message leg removed → `return issue !== undefined;`), anchor x1→x0, replacement x0→x1, blob `c886e177…` → `3cccd072c9cfe48685728086055cefef6cb7b52a` (the same mutated blob the round reported), 2026-09-22T23:14:11Z: **LIT red, DARK green** — `× LIT … AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1` at `build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts:4751:22`, which is `expect(status).toBe(1)`: the gate exited 0 and WAIVED the seeded deletion. That is the card's failure direction, 「reads as compliant」. Restore: blob `c886e177…` == `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty (MATCH).

**Ablation B** (refuses everything → `return false; // ablation-B`): anchor x1→x0, replacement x0→x1, blob `c886e177…` → `b67031b7f25fdbcfe3998d36461c2558964e3c9d`, 2026-09-22T23:15:59Z: **LIT green, DARK red** — `× DARK … AssertionError: expected '…' to contain 'carry their own proof (#4650)'` at `:4798`, i.e. the tree's own door, which does deliver its prescription, was refused anyway and the gate exited 1. Restore: blob `c886e177…` == `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty (MATCH). (The round did not run this arm; it inferred DARK's role from A. The inference was right, and it is now measured.)

Together: A shows the LIT case is red for exactly the waiver a lost message leg grants (and the DARK case, same box, same key, differing only in whether `strictObject` hands over its error map, stays green — so the box construction and the seeded key are sound and the red is not a fixture artefact); B shows the DARK case catches a gate that refuses everything. The pair separates 「reads the message」 from 「refuses everything」.

Could LIT go red for another reason? Its assertions after `status` also exclude the `not reachable from the` and `was LIVE (never tombstoned)` verdicts and the `prescribed` text, all of which exist as the gate's own strings at `origin/main:build-schemas.ts:2744–2759` (checked: the DARK string `carries the prescription its `strictObject` declaration owes` is on `:2745`, the LIT string `a `strictObject` declaration NAMES '…', but writing it` on `:2759`). A `beforeAll` failure would redden both cases; DARK's green under A rules that out.

**Full-harness ablation A (the reading the card's acceptance `5737129694` said must be taken before landing, and which the round's `85 skipped` did not take):** the whole harness, no `-t` filter, with `delivers()` at blob `3cccd072…` (message leg removed), 2026-09-22T23:16:20Z → 23:28:18Z, 716.94 s on my shared box: **`Tests 1 failed | 86 passed (87)`, exit 1** — the single red is the new LIT case at `:4751:22` and every one of the 85 pre-existing cases stayed green. Restore proven: blob `c886e177…` == `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` 0 lines; final intact re-run (23:14:58Z) 2 passed | 85 skipped, exit 0.

### 4. The fixture-validity assertions — the argument holds

`beforeAll` carries, before any box is built: (i) `pristineSurface` does not contain `system/ServerRateLimitConfig:keyBy` (re-derived on `origin/main`: 0 hits in `packages/spec/authorable-surface/`, firing control: `…:enabled`, `…:maxRequests`, `…:windowMs` present); (ii) the manifest still emits `system/ServerRateLimitConfig`; (iii) `keyBy` is not on `RateLimitConfigSchema.shape`; (iv) the real `ServerRateLimitConfigSchema` refuses `keyBy` AND its message carries `PRESCRIPTION_BULLET` (the DARK leg's tree fact); (v) `z.object(RateLimitConfigSchema.shape).strict()` refuses `keyBy` with an `unrecognized_keys` issue whose message does NOT carry the bullet. Assertion (v) is what makes this a pin on the MESSAGE half: it proves in-process that the probe DOES get an `unrecognized_keys` issue for the clone, so `&&` does not short-circuit and only `issue.message.includes(prescription)` can separate LIT from DARK. The existing `ui/ViewItem` pin (`origin/main:1123–1140`, `:1276–1290`) asserts the opposite — `not.toContain('unrecognized_keys')` — so it defends the left half only. The two pins are disjoint by their own assertions.

The substitution keeps `strictObjectError(options, shape)` and drops only the map: `strictObjectError` performs `declarationStore().push({ options, shape })` (`origin/main:strict-object.ts:346`) and `strictObject` is exactly `z.object(shape, { error: strictObjectError(options, shape) }).strict()` (`:357–359`, one 3-line declaration, so `STRICT_OBJECT_ANCHOR`'s lazy `[\s\S]*?\n\}\n` matches it and nothing else). Proof 4's `promisesFor` therefore still finds the promise, the door is still closed, and only the refusal text changes — the card's exact shape.

### 5. Cost — the reasoning is sound and the honest number is the one quoted

Arithmetic re-checked from the round's own figures: 646.38 − 632.50 = 13.88 s = 2.19 % of 632.50; 7.803 + 8.342 = 16.145 s = 2.50 % of 646.38; 625.88 − 623.31 = 2.57 s. The whole-run delta (13.88) is what the direct cost (16.14) minus the unchanged cases' negative drift (−2.57) predicts (13.57; the ~0.3 s remainder is hook time, consistent with the measured 351 ms `src` copy), so the two numbers agree rather than compete. The seat's argument that a single whole-run pair cannot RESOLVE a ~14 s effect is right on its own evidence (summed per-case absolute drift 31.05 s within the pair; the earlier measurement round saw 59.29 s between two byte-identical runs). The cost this review quotes is the resolvable one: **about two gate spawns, 16.1 s, ≈2.5 % of a harness run**. My own timings on the same two cases (7.6–10.1 s LIT, 7.1–9.3 s DARK across five runs on a shared box) sit in the same band. No fabricated percentage found; the whole-run delta is not quoted as the cost.

### 6. Clause-② and the changeset — declared `no`, and right

The declaration reads `no` on the card's live claim comment `5784429035` and on the PR body, both by `os-support-ai`. The path limb (`packages/spec/src/**` non-test) does not fire: the one path is `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts`. The content limb: the diff adds no key to any published payload, touches no `.zod.ts`, and the pack list is byte-identical to base (§2). The clause-② value `no` is correct for this diff.

`skip-changeset` was applied at 2026-09-22T23:04:33Z by `os-support-ai` (timeline event; the round's dev report says it applied no label, which is consistent). Route 0 discriminator re-run: `git diff --name-status c120dbdfb8 <head> -- '.changeset/*.md'` → 0 rows (firing control: the same instrument over `c120dbdfb8~30..c120dbdfb8` → 5 `A` rows; dark control on `.changesett/*.md` → 0). The gate's own job log (run `35795377021`, job `106973341647`, 23:03:33Z) prints route 2 as `2. It releases nothing (.github/, .claude/, skills/, docs/, content/, examples/, tests-only, and the like) -> apply the 'skip-changeset' label.   <<< PREFERRED` and `NOT this route if route 0 matched`. Route 0 did not match; the diff is tests-only and publishes nothing. The label is the right call. The newer `Check Changeset` run (`106974113468`, 23:04:36Z) concluded `skipped` on the label, as the workflow designs (`pr-automation.yml:290`, `:344–345`); the earlier `failure` (`106973341647`, 23:03:35Z) is the pre-label first run the workflow itself describes as the common case.

### 7. Gates — read from this head's check-runs, not re-run

Read from the head's check-runs (`GET /commits/cbb3521fe5eb…/check-runs`, polled until no run was pending; final read 2026-09-22T23:24:51Z): **39 check-runs, 0 pending**. Newest run per check name:
